title: Amendment 1 spec review: convergence rule, the fifth review is the last before hand-off
context: Four spec reviews of amendment 1 each found a new implementation that broke the rays recolour rule yet passed a fixed test sequence (partly built rays; glow-only change; first-composite-only and early-return; whole-palette comparison). The cause was structural: each fix added one case to a hand-written sequence, so every review could find the next missing case. The fifth revision replaced the sequence with an exhaustive check of the rule (every 3-operation sequence over five palettes and a step, from built and mask-only starts, 432 runs), proven to fail on the built change and all six flawed fixes found so far. The owner asked on 2026-10-13 that the reviews converge.
options: Make the fifth review the last: act only on findings that are a plausible implementation breaking the rule that the exhaustive test passes, a mismatch between the row and the draft test, or a gate or ship-gate defect; fix those, verify each with the probe, and hand off without a sixth review; record everything else as an accepted risk
Keep reviewing until a review returns no issues
option_reasons: The exhaustive test closes the rule as a whole, so only a concrete escape from it or a mechanical defect can still cause the wrong build; the build's round-2 review is the next independent check, and the pipeline verdict there stops a round that makes no progress
A reviewer told to find issues can always name another contrived case or wording point, so this has no end point, as the owner observed
outcome: Fifth review is the last before hand-off, under the stated filter. Findings outside it (contrived implementations, sequences longer than three operations needing call counting or test-specific palettes, wording that does not change what is built) go to the spec's assumptions and the final report as accepted risks. Round 2 of the build review converges through pipeline.mjs verdict: a round whose blockers are not fewer than the last one's stops the loop.
